records.summary: The Arnesian Jungle is the humid, forested upland of the north-east, between Thorn on the coast and the mesa country to the south. It is the Stone-Sleepers' country: stone-built hamlets and a terraced city, a long inlet from the bay, Velothi ruins on the shores and a corner of Warden forts and camps round Thorn.
records.landform: Low forested uplands cut by a long tidal inlet from Thorn's bay, with rises, river terraces and shores
records.biome: Humid lowland jungle and riverine forest, with grassland at the Thorn end
records.climate: Warm, humid, with heavy summer rain and sea fog on the coast

notes.text: The Arnesian Jungle takes its name from Arnesia, the east-coast country around Thorn and Archon, a settlement and region near both cities.

sources.title: Arnesian Jungle: UESP's Lore:Arnesia and the 4E 201 state document
ARNESIAN JUNGLE label sits north of Tsonac, with the long inlet, Thorn and Tsonac on the map

notes.text: Barsaebic Ayleids and Cantemiric Velothi settled the country around Arnesia, Archon and Thorn before their extinction. The Arnesian War of 3E 396 began as a slave revolt in southern Dres lands and ended with Morrowind annexing Arnesia; from 3E 432 the Argonians began to reclaim the ground, and slavers were still active in Arnesia in the late Third Era.
In 4E 201 the jungle is the Stone-Sleepers' home country, with Tsonac as capital and the Warden forts, camps and posts stand round Thorn at its coastal edge.

notes.text: Mostly Stone-Sleeper Argonians, with Root-Folk hunters, Warden garrisons and field-owners' crews near Thorn and Dunmer traders on the road.

sources.title: Arnesian Jungle: UESP's Lore:Arnesia and the 4E 201 state document

notes.text: Timber, quarried stone, hides and sap, sold to Thorn; saltrice and tools come back.

notes.text: The sky-blue people hold their city's Hist to be asleep; hamlets keep cairns for it, while the Root-Folk keep their own trees.

notes.text: Terraced stone towns among tall hardwoods, a broad bay inlet with muddy banks, Velothi ruins under vines.

sources.title: Arnesian Jungle: UESP's Lore:Arnesia and the 4E 201 state document

notes.text: Risky away from roads and dangerous at the Velothi ruins. The Thorn road and the towns are mostly safe.

notes.text: A long inlet from the bay runs west to Tsonac, with rivers branching off to the south and north-west; rises of 30 to 60 m stand between them, and the ground is marshy at the shore.

notes.text: Jungle hardwood, tree-ferns, vines and bright fungus; mudcrabs and slaughterfish along the banks and in the inlet, giant snakes and giant spiders inland, grass and saltrice near Thorn.

notes.text: Hot and wet: rain and fog are the commonest weathers, with clear spells that come and go by chance.

records.summary: Chixathe Mesa is a high, dry, flat-topped upland south of the Arnesian Jungle, with cliff edges, quarries and chalk pits, Velothi ruins and a Sarpa-held western edge. It is the quarry country of the Stone-Sleepers and the Wardens.
records.landform: Flat-topped mesas with cliff sides, cut by rivers, with quarries and chalk faces
records.biome: Dry upland scrub and stunted forest on the mesa tops, riverine jungle in the cuts
records.climate: Warm and drier than the jungle, with sharp winds on the heights

notes.text: Chixathe Mesa lies between the Arnesian country and the Middle Argonian interior.

sources.title: Chixathe Mesa: no UESP page; Velothi, Sarpa and Stone-Sleeper facts
CHIXATHE MESA label sits at the mesa's centre on the map

notes.text: The Cantemiric Velothi settled the east of Black Marsh before the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560-603 killed them; their ruins at Kaochalit, Balormaak and Vorannuhl stand on the mesa.

In 4E 201 it is a thin, mixed country: Stone-Sleeper hamlets and quarries to the north and east, Warden fort at Chalkmoth, Root-Folk and Sedge-Warden outposts, an Agaceph hamlet in the south and Sarpa on the western edge.

notes.text: No single culture: Stone-Sleepers, Root-Folk, Agaceph, Sedge-Wardens and Clay-Mound families, with Sarpa to the west.

notes.text: Chixathe Mesa yields quarried stone, chalk and lime, hides and books, sent off the mesa to Thorn and the river towns.

notes.text: A mix of Hist customs: the Sarpa keep their own tree beyond the edge, the Stone-Sleepers raise cairns for Tsonac's sleeping Hist and the Agaceph read their mission books at hatchings.

notes.text: Pale cliffs and flat tops, white chalk dust, stone cuts, rivers in green gorges.

notes.text: Dangerous away from roads: Sarpa raiders, Velothi undead and cliff falls.

notes.text: Flat mesa tops 60 to 110 m above the lowland, cliffs on the edges and river gorges between them.

notes.text: Scrub, tall grass and thorn-bush on the tops; crocodiles, giant snakes, hawks and giant spiders in the gorges and the Sarpa on the western edge.

notes.text: Drier than the jungle; the mesa tops hold little water and cold nights follow hot days.
